**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 37, verses 7–11:**

﴿And as a guard﴾, meaning: We guarded them with a complete guard ﴿against every rebellious devil﴾, who is defiant and disobedient. They are pelted with them (the stars).

﴿So that they cannot listen﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read *yassamma'una* (يَسَّمَّعُونَ) with a doubled sin and mim. The meaning is *la yatasamma'una* (لَا يَتَسَمَّعُونَ), "they do not eavesdrop", and the ta' was assimilated into the sin (*idgham*, assimilation of letters). The other readers (*qira'at*) read it with a sukun on the sin and a light mim. ﴿To the exalted assembly﴾, meaning: to the scribes among the angels.

The "exalted assembly" (*al-mala' al-a'la*, الملأ الأعلى) are the angels, because they are in the heavens. The meaning is that they are unable to listen to the exalted assembly. ﴿And they are pelted﴾, meaning they are struck, ﴿from every direction﴾, from the horizons of the heaven, with shooting stars.

﴿Repulsed﴾: they are kept away from the gatherings of the angels. It is said: *dahharahu dahran wa duhuran* (دَحَرَهُ دَحْرًا وَدُحُورًا), meaning when he drove him away and removed him. ﴿And for them is a perpetual punishment﴾.

Muqatil said: "perpetual" means until the first blast, because they are burned and driven mad (*yatakhabbalun*).

﴿Except one who snatches a fragment﴾, meaning he steals a word from the speech of the angels by stealth. ﴿Then he is pursued﴾, meaning he is overtaken, ﴿by a piercing flame﴾.

A bright, powerful star that does not miss; it kills him, or burns him, or drives him mad. They return to eavesdropping, though they know they cannot reach it, out of hope for safety and attaining their aim, like the rider of the sea. 'Ata' said: the star with which the devils are struck is called "piercing" (*thaqib*, ثاقب) because it pierces them.

﴿So ask them﴾, meaning: ask them, that is the people of Makkah, ﴿are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾, meaning: from the heavens, the earth and the mountains. This is a question meaning affirmation (*taqrir*, تقرير): these things are stronger in creation, as He said: ﴿Certainly the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57], and He said: ﴿Are you stronger in creation, or is the heaven? He built it﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 27].

It is also said: "or those whom We have created" means from the past nations, because *man* (مَنْ) is used for those who have reason. The meaning: these people are not stronger in creation than other nations, and We destroyed them for their sins, so what will secure these people from punishment? Then He mentioned the creation of man, and said:

﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾, meaning: good, pure clay that adheres, that clings to the hand. Its meaning is "the binding" (*al-lazim*, اللازم). The mim was changed to a ba', as if it binds the hand. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it is foul-smelling (*muntin*).

Qur'anic quotations: "بَلْ عَجِبْتَ" — "Nay, you marvel" (ﷺ-directed reading). Let me translate the passage now.

**"Nay, you marvel"** — Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with a dammah on the tā' (ʿajibtu → ʿujibta, i.e., "you are amazed" in the passive-causative sense), and this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas. The marvelling of Allah, mighty and majestic, is not like the marvelling of human beings, as He says: "﴿So they mock them; Allah mocks them﴾" [al-Tawbah: 79], and He says: "﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾" [al-Tawbah: 67]. So the marvelling of human beings is their disapproval and their magnification (of something), whereas the marvelling of Allah, exalted is He, may carry the meaning of disapproval and blame, and may carry the meaning of approval and being pleased, as has come in the hadith: "Your Lord marvels at a young man who has no inclination toward youthful folly" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 4/151. Ibn al-Dayba' al-Shaybani said in Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith (p. 51): "al-Qada'i narrated it in his Musnad from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah with its chain from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ). It is likewise in Ahmad and Abu Ya'la, and its chain is good, though Ibn Hajar weakened it because of Ibn Lahi'ah."]].

And there came in the hadith: "Your Lord marvels at your asking and your despairing and the swiftness of His response to you" [[In the printed edition: "Your Lord marvels at your al-'all..." Abu 'Ubayd narrated it in al-Gharib from Muhammad ibn 'Umar, raised, then said: "al-Al" is raising the voice in supplication, and some narrate it as al-Awwal, which means severity. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 141.]].

It was narrated that al-Junayd was asked about this verse, and he said: "Indeed Allah does not marvel at anything, but Allah agreed with His Messenger when His Messenger marvelled, so He said: '﴿But if you marvel, then marvellous is their saying﴾' [al-Ra'd: 5]," meaning: it is as you say.

The others read it with a fatḥah on the tā', addressing the Prophet ﷺ, meaning: you marvel at their denying you, "﴿and they mock﴾" at your marvelling.

Qatadah said: The Prophet ﷺ marvelled at this Qur'an when it was revealed and at the misguidance of the children of Adam [[See: al-Tabari 23/44; al-Durr al-Manthur 7/83; Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/5.]]. That was because the Prophet ﷺ used to think that everyone who heard the Qur'an would believe in it. When the polytheists heard the Qur'an, they mocked it and did not believe in it, so the Prophet ﷺ marvelled at that. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: "﴿Nay, you marvel, and they mock﴾."

"﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾" — meaning: when they are admonished with the Qur'an, they do not heed.

"﴿And when they see a sign﴾" — Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: this refers to the splitting of the moon. "﴿they mock﴾" — they scoff and ridicule. It was also said: some of them solicit mockery from one another.

"﴿And they say: This is nothing but manifest magic﴾" — [meaning: clear magic].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 16–24:

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again?﴾

﴿And our forefathers of old?﴾ That is: and our first forefathers too.

﴿Say: Yes, and you will be humbled.﴾ You will be raised, and you will be ﴿humbled﴾ (ṣāghirūn), and humiliation (al-duxūr) is the greatest abasement.

﴿It will be but a single shout.﴾ That is: the matter of the Resurrection or the Last Day. ﴿A shout﴾ means a cry, ﴿single﴾ meaning the blast of resurrection. ﴿Then behold, they will be looking on﴾, alive.

﴿They will say: Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.﴾ That is: the Day of Reckoning and the Day of Recompense.

﴿This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny.﴾ It is the Day of Judgment. It is also said: it is the Day of Distinction between the good-doer and the evildoer.

﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾, that is, those who associated partners with God. Gather them to the place of standing for reckoning and recompense. ﴿And their companions﴾ means their counterparts, their followers, and their like.

Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: whoever did a deed like theirs, so the people of wine are with the people of wine, and the people of fornication are with the people of fornication.

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: their companions among the devils, each disbeliever with his devil in a chain. Al-Hasan said: ﴿and their companions﴾ means their polytheist wives.

﴿And what they used to worship besides God﴾ in the world, that is, the idols and the tyrants. Muqatil said: it means Iblis and his armies, and he cited the verse: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?﴾ [Yasin: 60].

﴿So guide them to the path of Hell.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: direct them to the road of the Fire. Ibn Kaysan said: lead them forward. The Arabs call the one who goes ahead a guide (hadi).

﴿And stop them﴾, that is, detain them. It is said: "I stopped him (waqaftuhu) a stop (waqfan), so he stopped (waqafa) and came to a standstill (wuqufan)."

The commentators said: when they are driven to the Fire, they are detained at the Sirat, because questioning takes place at the Sirat. So it is said: ﴿stop them, for they are to be questioned.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: about all their words and deeds.

It is narrated from him (Ibn Abbas), concerning: "There is no god but God." In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about four things: about his youth, how he spent it; about his life, how he consumed it; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and how he spent it; and about his knowledge, what he did with it." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Qiyamah, chapter: What has come concerning the reckoning and retribution: 7/101, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Mundhiri endorsed it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, and al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/346) attributed a similar version to al-Tabarani and al-Bazzar, then said: "The narrators of al-Tabarani are the narrators of the Sahih apart from Samit ibn Mu'adh and Adi ibn Adi al-Kindi, and both are trustworthy."]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verse 25–29:

﴿What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?﴾ That is: you do not help one another. It is said to them as a rebuke: "What is the matter with you that one of you does not help the other?" The keepers of the Fire will say this to them. This is a reply to Abu Jahl, when he said on the Day of Badr: "We are a united force that will be victorious" [al-Qamar: 44].

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Rather, they are today submitting (mustaslimun)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Humbled (khadi'un)." Al-Hasan said: "Submissive (munqadun)." It is said: "istaslama lil-shay'" means he yielded to the thing and was subdued by it. The meaning is: they are today abased and submissive, with no recourse.

﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾: that is, the leaders and the followers, ﴿questioning﴾ means disputing with one another.

﴿They will say﴾: that is, the followers to the leaders, ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right (al-yamin)﴾: that is, from the direction of religion, so you misguided us from it [and made us see that the religion is not that with which you misguided us]. [[In "B": "and you turned us back to that with which you misguided us."]] This was said by al-Dahhak. Mujahid said: "from the straight path of truth." Al-yamin is an expression for religion and truth, as Allah the Exalted reported about Iblis: "Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left" [al-A'raf: 17]. Thus whoever is approached by Satan from the direction of the right is approached from the direction of religion, and he confuses the truth for him.

Some of them said: the leaders used to swear oaths to them that what they called them to was the truth. So the meaning of His saying "you used to come to us from the right" is: from the side of the oaths that you used to swear, so we trusted them.

It was also said: "from the right" means: from strength and power, as in His saying: "We would have seized him by the right hand" [al-Haqqah: 45]. But the exegetes follow the first opinion.

﴿They will say﴾, meaning the leaders [[In "B": the messengers.]] to the followers: ﴿Rather, you were not believers﴾: you were not upon the truth, so we misguided you from it. That is: the disbelief came from you.

It is said to them as a rebuke: "What is the matter with you that one of you does not help the other?" The keepers of the Fire will say this to them. This is a reply to Abu Jahl, when he said on the Day of Badr: "We are a united force that will be victorious" [al-Qamar: 44].

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Rather, they are today submitting (mustaslimun)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Humbled (khadi'un)." Al-Hasan said: "Submissive (munqadun)." It is said: "istaslama lil-shay'" means he yielded to the thing and was subdued by it. The meaning is: they are today abased and submissive, with no recourse.

﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾: that is, the leaders and the followers, ﴿questioning﴾ means disputing with one another.

﴿They will say﴾: that is, the followers to the leaders, ﴿Indeed, you used to come to us from the right (al-yamin)﴾: that is, from the direction of religion, so you misguided us from it [and made us see that the religion is not that with which you misguided us]. [[In "B": "and you turned us back to that with which you misguided us."]] This was said by al-Dahhak. Mujahid said: "from the straight path of truth." Al-yamin is an expression for religion and truth, as Allah the Exalted reported about Iblis: "Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left" [al-A'raf: 17]. Thus whoever is approached by Satan from the direction of the right is approached from the direction of religion, and he confuses the truth for him.

Some of them said: the leaders used to swear oaths to them that what they called them to was the truth. So the meaning of His saying "you used to come to us from the right" is: from the side of the oaths that you used to swear, so we trusted them.

It was also said: "from the right" means: from strength and power, as in His saying: "We would have seized him by the right hand" [al-Haqqah: 45]. But the exegetes follow the first opinion.

﴿They will say﴾, meaning the leaders [[In "B": the messengers.]] to the followers: ﴿Rather, you were not believers﴾: you were not upon the truth, so we misguided you from it. That is: the disbelief came from you.

﴿So the word of our Lord has come into effect against us﴾, meaning it became binding upon us all, ﴿the word of our Lord﴾, that is, the word of punishment, which is His saying: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together" [As-Sajdah: 13]. ﴿Indeed, we are to taste [the punishment]﴾, meaning that the one who goes astray and the one who leads astray are all in the Fire.

﴿So we misled you﴾, meaning we led you astray from guidance and invited you to what we ourselves were upon, ﴿for indeed, we were ourselves astray﴾, meaning misguided. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So on that Day they will be sharers in the punishment﴾, meaning the leaders and the followers.

﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: those who set up partners with Allah.

﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," were arrogant﴾, meaning they were too proud to accept the word of monotheism and refused it.

﴿And they said, "Shall we leave our gods for a mad poet?"﴾, meaning the Prophet (ﷺ).

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in response to them: ﴿Rather, he has come with the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾, meaning that he brought what the messengers before him had brought.

﴿Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾ in the world, namely shirk.

﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾, meaning those who affirm His oneness.

﴿For those, there will be a known provision﴾, meaning morning and evening [as He said: "And for them there is their provision therein, morning and evening" [Maryam: 62]] [[The text between the brackets is omitted in manuscript "B".]].

﴿Fawakih﴾ is the plural of fakihah, which means all fruits, both fresh and dried. It refers to any food eaten for enjoyment rather than for sustenance. ﴿And they will be honoured﴾ with the reward of Allah.

﴿In Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another﴾, so that none of them sees the back of another.

﴿They will be served with a cup﴾, meaning a vessel containing drink. It is not called a cup (ka's) unless it contains drink; otherwise it is merely a vessel. ﴿From a flowing spring﴾, meaning wine flowing in rivers, manifest, which the eyes can see.

﴿White﴾. Al-Hasan said: the wine of Paradise is whiter than milk. ﴿Delicious﴾, meaning delightful. ﴿To those who drink﴾.

﴿No headache will it cause, nor will they be intoxicated by it﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: it does not seize their minds so as to take them away. Al-Kalbi said: sin. Qatadah said: stomach pain. Al-Hasan said: headache.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani, the linguists and scholars of semantics) said: al-ghawl is a corruption that befalls a person in secret. It is said: "ightālahu ightiyālan" when he ruined his affair for him secretly. The wine of this world produces various kinds of corruption, including intoxication and loss of reason, stomach pain, headache, vomiting, and urination. None of these occurs in the wine of Paradise.

﴿Nor will they be drained of it﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yunzifun" with a kasra on the zay (a qira'ah, a recognised mode of reciting the Qur'an), and 'Asim agreed with them in al-Waqi'ah. The others read it with a fatha on the zay in both places. Whoever reads with a fatha means: it will not overpower their minds, and they will not become drunk. It is said: "nazafa al-rajul fa-huwa manzuf wa nazif" when a man becomes drunk. Whoever reads with a kasra means: their drink will not run out. It is said: "anzafa al-rajul fa-huwa manzuf" when his wine has run out.

﴿And with them will be maidens restraining their gaze﴾, meaning restraining their eyes and lowering their eyelids. They have confined their eyes to their husbands and do not look at anyone else. ﴿With beautiful, large eyes﴾, meaning having fine eyes. It is said: "rajul a'yan" for a man, "imra'ah 'aynā'" for a woman, and "nisa' 'in" for women.

﴿As if they were eggs﴾ [plural of bayd(ah)] [[Addition from "b".]] ﴿well-guarded﴾, meaning protected and concealed. He mentioned "al-maknun" and "al-bayd" in the plural because he returned it to the wording (lafz) [of the verse].

Al-Hasan said: He likened them to the eggs of the ostrich, which are sheltered with feathers from wind and dust, so their colour is white with a yellowish tinge. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 37, verses 50–59:**

﴿Then some of them turned to others, questioning one another.﴾ That is, the people of Paradise, in Paradise, ask one another about their condition in the world.

﴿One of them said﴾, that is, one of the people of Paradise: ﴿"Indeed, I had a companion﴾ in the world who denied the Resurrection (al-Ba'th).

Mujahid said: he was a devil. Others said: he was a human being.[[See: al-Tabari 23/58.]] Muqatil said: they were two brothers. Others said: they were two partners, one of them a disbeliever named Qatrus and the other a believer named Yahudha. These are the two whose story Allah Most High relates in Surah al-Kahf,[[See above: note (4): 5/170.]] in His saying: ﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾ [al-Kahf: 32].

﴿He would say: "Are you indeed among those who affirm?"﴾ That is, of the Resurrection.

﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be recompensed?"﴾ That is, shall we be requited and called to account? This is a rhetorical question expressing denial.

﴿He said﴾: Allah Most High says to the people of Paradise: ﴿"Would you like to look down?"﴾ into the Fire. It was also said: the believer says to his brothers among the people of Paradise: "Would you like to look down into the Fire, so that we may see how my brother's station is?" And the people of Paradise say: "You know him better than we do."

﴿So he looked down﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: indeed in Paradise there are openings through which its people look at the Fire.[[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 7/94; Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/9. The statement in both is attributed to Kaʿb al-Ahbar.]] So this believer looked down, ﴿and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾, that is, he saw his companion in the middle of the Fire. The middle of a thing is called sawāʾ only because its sides are equal (istiwāʾ al-jawānib).

﴿He said﴾ to him: ﴿"By Allah, you nearly ruined me!﴾ By Allah, you nearly caused me to perish. Muqatil said: "By Allah, you nearly led me astray," and whoever leads a person astray has destroyed him.

﴿"Had it not been for the favour of my Lord﴾, that is, His mercy and His bounty upon me through Islam, ﴿I would certainly have been among those brought forth﴾ [to the punishment] along with you in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 60–66:

﴿They will say, "Indeed, this is the great triumph."﴾ It was also said: they say it by way of recounting the blessing of Allah upon them, that they will not die and will not be punished. And it was said: the believer says it to his companion by way of rebuke for what he used to deny [[Mentioned by the author of al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/362.]].

Allah Most High said: ﴿For the like of this let the workers work.﴾ That is: for the like of this abode and this bliss, which He mentioned in His words: "Those will have a known provision" up to "let the workers work."

﴿Is that better as a welcome or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾ That is: is that which was mentioned for the people of Paradise better, or the tree of al-Zaqqum, which is the welcome of the people of the Fire? Al-Zaqqum is the fruit of a wicked tree, bitter and foul-tasting, and the people of the Fire are compelled to eat it, so they swallow it (yatazaqqamuna) with the utmost loathing. From this comes the saying: "tazaqqama al-ta'am" (he swallowed the food) when he took it reluctantly and with difficulty.

﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the disbelievers. That is because they said: "How can there be a tree in the Fire, when the Fire burns trees?" Ibn al-Za'bara said to the chieftains of Quraysh: "Muhammad frightens us with al-Zaqqum, and al-Zaqqum in the language of the Berbers means butter and dates." Abu Jahl brought them into his house and said: "O slave girl, give us zaqqum!" So she brought them butter and dates, and he said: "Eat zaqqum! This is what Muhammad threatens you with" [[See: al-Tabari: 23/63.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verse 67–77:

﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture﴾ (shawb): a blend and admixture ﴿of boiling water﴾ (hamim): water that is hot and extremely scalding. It is said that when they eat the zaqqum, it is said to them: "Drink over it the boiling water." So the boiling water mixes in their bellies with the zaqqum, and it becomes a mixture for them.

﴿Then indeed their return﴾ after drinking the boiling water [﴿is surely to the Blazing Fire﴾. This is because they are brought to the boiling water to drink from it while it is outside the Fire, just as camels are brought to water, and then they are returned to the Blazing Fire.] [[What is between the brackets is omitted in "A".]] This is indicated by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They will go around between it and boiling water, intensely hot﴾ [al-Rahman: 44]. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "Then indeed their resting place is surely to the Blazing Fire."

﴿Indeed they found﴾ (alfa'): they found ﴿their fathers astray﴾.

﴿So they, upon their footsteps, are hastened﴾ (yuhra'un): they hasten. Al-Kalbi said: they act like their actions.

﴿And already before them had strayed most of the former peoples﴾: from the earlier nations that passed away.

﴿And We had already sent among them warners. So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾: the disbelievers; that is, their end was punishment.

﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾: the monotheists, who were saved from the punishment.

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Nuh had certainly called to Us﴾: he supplicated his Lord against his people, saying: "Indeed I am overpowered, so help [me]" [al-Qamar: 10]. ﴿And how excellent are We as responders﴾: meaning, We answered his supplication and destroyed his people.

﴿And We saved him and his family from the great distress﴾ [the great grief] [[Omitted in "A".]] which befell his people, namely the drowning.

﴿And We made his descendants the surviving ones﴾: and He intends that all people are from the offspring of Nuh.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Nuh came out of the ark, every man and woman who was with him died except his sons and their wives [in "B": and his wives].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The sons of Nuh were three: Sam, Ham, and Yafith. Sam is the father of the Arabs, Persians, and Romans; Ham is the father of the Sudanese; and Yafith is the father of the Turks, the Khazars, Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and what is beyond them. [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir: 4 / 13.]]

﴿And he said﴾, that is, Abraham: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾, meaning: I am emigrating to my Lord. The sense is: I abandon the abode of disbelief and go to the pleasure of my Lord. He said this after coming out of the fire, just as he said: "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord" [al-'Ankabut: 26]. ﴿He will guide me﴾ to the place where He commanded me to go, which is al-Sham (Syria).

Muqatil said: When he arrived in the Holy Land, he asked his Lord for a child, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾, meaning: grant me a righteous son from among the righteous.

﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy﴾. It was said: a boy in his youth, forbearing in his old age. In this there is good news that he would be a son, that he would live and reach an age at which he would be described as forbearing.

﴿And when he reached with him the age of exertion﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: it means walking with him to the mountain. Mujahid reported from Ibn 'Abbas: when he grew up and reached the point where his effort was like Ibrahim's effort [Narrated by al-Tabari: 23/77]. The meaning is: he reached the point of being able to act with him and help him in his work. Al-Kalbi said: it means the work for Allah, the Exalted, and this is the view of al-Hasan, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Ibn Zayd, who said: it is worship of Allah, the Exalted.

They differed about his age. It was said: he was thirteen years old. It was also said: he was seven years old.

﴿He said: O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you﴾. The scholars among the Muslims differed about this boy whom Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice, after the People of the Two Books (Jews and Christians) agreed that he was Ishaq (Isaac). One group said: he was Ishaq, and this view was held by the Companions (sahaba): 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas; and among the Successors (tabi'un) and those who followed them: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, Ikrimah, 'Ata', Muqatil, al-Zuhri and al-Suddi. This is also the narration of Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr [from Ibn 'Abbas], and they said: this incident took place in al-Sham. [The text between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: Ibrahim was shown in a dream the sacrifice of Ishaq [See above: 4/215, note (1)], so he set out with him for a distance of a month in one morning until he brought him to the place of sacrifice at Mina. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, at the beginning of Islam the head of the ram was indeed hanging by its horns in the spout of the Ka'bah, dried out (wahasha), meaning it had dried up."

Al-Asma'i said: I asked Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' about the sacrificed one: was it Ishaq or Isma'il? He said: "O Sumay', where has your mind gone? When was Ishaq in Makkah? It was Isma'il who was in Makkah, and he is the one who built the House with his father."

As for the story of the sacrifice, al-Suddi said: When Ibrahim prayed, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾, and was given good news of him, he said: "Then he is indeed a sacrifice for Allah." When he was born and reached the age of exertion, he was told: "Fulfill your vow." This is the reason for Allah's command to him to sacrifice his son. At that point he said to Ishaq: "Go and offer a sacrifice to Allah, the Exalted." He took a knife and a rope and set out with him until he took him between the mountains. The boy said to him: "O father, where is your sacrifice?" He said: "﴿O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think﴾." He said: "﴿O my father, do as you are commanded﴾."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Whenever Ibrahim visited Hajar and Isma'il, he was carried on al-Buraq. He would set out in the morning from al-Sham and take a midday rest in Makkah, and in the afternoon he would leave Makkah and spend the night with his family in al-Sham. When Isma'il reached the age of exertion with him, and had become self-reliant, and Ibrahim hoped for him because of what he expected of him in worshipping his Lord and honoring His sacred things, he was commanded in a dream to sacrifice him. This was because on the night of al-Tarwiyah he saw as if someone was saying to him: "Indeed Allah commands you to sacrifice this son of yours." When he woke in the morning, he pondered in himself, that is, he reflected from morning until afternoon: "Is this dream from Allah or from Satan?" For this reason that day was called the Day of Tarwiyah (reflection). When he entered the evening, he saw the dream again. When he woke in the morning, he knew that it was from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason that day was called the Day of 'Arafah (knowledge).

Muqatil said: Ibrahim saw this for three consecutive nights. When he became certain of it, he told his son, saying: "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think."

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "tura" (ﵟ ﵞ, "see what you think") with a damma on the taa' and a kasra on the raa', meaning "what do you indicate?" Ibrahim only commanded him so that He would know his patience in obeying Allah's command and his resolve in obeying Him.

The majority read it with a fatha on the taa' and the raa', except Abu 'Amr, who inclined the raa' (imalah).

His son said to him: ﴿O my father, do as you are commanded﴾. Ibn Ishaq and others said: When Ibrahim was commanded to do this, he said to his son: "O my son, take the rope and the knife, and let us go to this ravine to gather firewood." When Ibrahim was alone with his son in the ravine of Thabir, he informed him of what he had been commanded. ﴿He said: O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verse 103:

﴿When they had both submitted﴾, they yielded and humbled themselves to the command of Allah the Exalted. Qatadah said: Ibrahim submitted his son, and the son submitted himself. ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾, that is, he threw him down onto the ground. Ibn Abbas said: He laid him on his side on the ground, with the forehead between the two temples. They said: His son, whom he intended to slaughter, said to him: "O father, tighten my bonds so that I do not thrash about, and keep your garments away from me so that none of my blood splashes onto them and my reward is diminished, and my mother sees it and grieves. Sharpen your blade and pass the knife swiftly over my throat so that it will be easier for me, for death is severe. When you come to my mother, convey my greetings to her, and if you see fit to return my shirt to my mother, do so, for it may be a consolation to her concerning me." Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to him: "What an excellent helper you are, my son, in the matter of Allah's command." So Ibrahim did what his son had instructed him. Then he turned to him, kissed him, while he had bound him, and he was weeping [and the son also was weeping]. Then he placed the knife upon his throat, but the knife did not cut.

It is also related that he began to drag the blade across his throat, but it did not cut. So he sharpened it twice or three times on the stone, and every time he was unable.

Al-Suddi said: Allah the Exalted struck a plate of copper upon his throat. They said: Then the son said at that moment: "O father, turn me onto my face upon my forehead, for if you look into my face you will have mercy on me and tenderness will overcome you, preventing you from carrying out the command of Allah the Exalted. And I do not look at the blade, lest I become distressed." So Ibrahim did that, then placed the blade upon his neck, and the knife turned over, and it was called out: "O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision."

Abu Hurayrah related from Ka'b al-Ahbar and Ibn Ishaq from his narrators, who said: When Ibrahim resolved to slaughter his son, Satan said: "If I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this point, I will never tempt any of them ever." So Satan took the form of a man and came to the boy's mother and said to her: "Do you know where Ibrahim has taken your son?" She said: "He has taken him to gather firewood from this valley." He said: "No, by Allah, he has taken him only to slaughter him." She said: "Certainly not. He is more merciful to him and loves him more intensely than that." He said: "He claims that Allah has commanded him to do so." She said: "If his Lord has commanded him to do so, then he has done well to obey his Lord." So Satan left her and caught up with the boy as he walked behind his father, and said to him: "O boy, do you know where your father is taking you?" He said: "We are going to gather firewood for our family from this valley." He said: "By Allah, he only intends to slaughter you." He said: "Why?" He said: "He claims that his Lord has commanded him to do so." He said: "Then let him do what his Lord has commanded him, hearing and obeying." When the boy refused him, he turned to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and said: "Where are you going, O old man?" He said: "I am going to this valley for a need of mine there." He said: "By Allah, I see that Satan has come to you in your sleep and commanded you to slaughter this son of yours." Ibrahim, peace be upon him, recognised him and said: "Away from me, O enemy of Allah! By Allah, I will certainly carry out the command of my Lord." So Iblis returned in rage, having achieved nothing of what he intended against Ibrahim and his family, for they had been protected from him by the help of Allah the Exalted. [Related by al-Tabari: 23/82; see also al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/110-111, Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/16-17.]

Abu al-Tufayl related from Ibn Abbas that when Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son, Satan appeared to him at this place and raced him, and Ibrahim outstripped him. Then he went to the Jamrat al-Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he pelted him with seven pebbles until he departed. Then he appeared to him at the Middle Jamrah, and he pelted him with seven pebbles until he departed. Then he caught up with him at the Greater Jamrah, and he pelted him with seven pebbles until he departed. Then Ibrahim proceeded to obey the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. [Related by al-Tabari: 23/80.]

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "So when they had both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 104–107:

﴿And We called to him﴾. The wāw in "wa-nādaynāhu" (وَنَادَيْنَاهُ) is an inserted, connective particle (muqhamah ṣilah). Its sense is: "We called to him," as in His saying: "And they agreed to put him into the depths of the well, and We revealed to him" [Yusuf: 15], meaning: "We revealed to him." So he was called from the mountain: ﴿O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision﴾. The speech ends here, then He begins: ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾. The meaning is: Just as We pardoned Ibrahim from slaughtering his son, so do We reward those who do good in obeying Us. Muqatil said: "Allah rewarded him for his good obedience with the pardon from slaughtering his son."

﴿Indeed, this is surely the manifest trial﴾. The "manifest test" is the clear examination, in that He tested him by the slaughter of his son. Muqatil said: "The trial (al-bala') here means the blessing, which is that his son was ransomed with the ram."

If it is asked: how did He say "you have fulfilled the vision," when he had seen himself slaughtering and had not slaughtered?

It is answered: He made him one who fulfilled it, because he had done what was within his power, and what was required of them both was submission to the command of Allah the Exalted, and they had done it.

It is also said: He had seen in sleep the hurrying of the slaughter but had not seen the shedding of blood, and he did in wakefulness what he had seen in sleep. Therefore He said to him: "You have fulfilled the vision."

﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾. Ibrahim looked, and behold, there was Jibril with him a white ram with curved horns. He said: "This is a ransom for your son, so slaughter it instead of him." Jibril said Allahu akbar, the ram said Allahu akbar, and his son said Allahu akbar. Ibrahim took the ram and brought it to the place of sacrifice at Mina and slaughtered it.

Most of the exegetes said: that ram had grazed in Paradise for forty years [Reported by al-Tabari: 23/87, from Ibn Abbas; al-Suyuti also attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/113 to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]

And it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The ram that Ibrahim slaughtered was the one that Adam's son Habil had offered." [Reported by al-Tabari: 23/86.]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It was right that it should be great." Mujahid said: "He called it great because it was accepted." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "Because it was from Allah." It was also said: "Great in its physical form." And it was said: "Great in reward."

Al-Hasan said: "Ismail was ransomed only with a wild mountain goat, which descended upon him from Thabir." [Reported by al-Tabari: 23/87, and Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir: 4/17.]

﴿And We left for him among later generations﴾: that is, We left for him among the later ones a good commendation.

The Qur'anic verse "And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers" (﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾)

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Ilyas is Idris." In his codex (mushaf) the reading is: "And indeed Idris was among the messengers." This is also the view of Ikrimah.

Others said: he was a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel.

Ibn Abbas said: he was the paternal cousin of al-Yasa' (Elisha).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: he was Ilyas ibn Bishr ibn Finhas ibn al-Ayzar ibn Harun ibn Imran.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq also said, and so did the scholars among the Ahl al-Akhbar (transmitters of historical reports): When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took the soul of the prophet Hizqil (Ezekiel) (ﷺ), the transgressions among the Children of Israel grew severe, corruption and polytheism appeared among them, and they set up idols and worshipped them besides Allah. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Ilyas to them as a prophet. The prophets from among the Children of Israel had been sent after Musa (Moses) to renew what they had forgotten of the Torah. The Children of Israel were scattered throughout the land of Shaam (Greater Syria). The reason for this was that Yushi' ibn Nun (Joshua), when he conquered Shaam, settled the Children of Israel in it and divided it among them. He settled one tribe of them in Ba'labakk and its surrounding areas, and these were the tribe from which Ilyas came. Allah the Exalted sent him to them as a prophet. At that time over them was a king called Ajab, who had led his people astray and compelled them to worship idols. He and his people worshipped an idol called Ba'l. Its height was twenty cubits, and it had four faces. Ilyas began calling them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but they would not listen to him at all, except that the king alone believed him and affirmed him. So Ilyas would set the king's affairs right, guide him and direct him.

This Ajab the king had a wife called Azbil, whom he would appoint as his deputy over his subjects whenever he was absent from them on a raid or for other reasons. She would appear before the people and judge between them. She was a killer of prophets; it is said that she was the one who killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah), peace be upon them both. She had a secretary, a wise believing man who concealed his faith. He had rescued from her hand three hundred prophets whom she wanted to kill, each one of them whenever he was sent, apart from those she had already killed. She was not chaste in herself. She had married seven kings of the Children of Israel and had killed all of them by assassination. She was long-lived; it is said she bore seventy children.

Ajab had a neighbour, a righteous man called Mazdaki, who had a garden from which he made his living and which he tended and maintained with care. The garden was next to the palace of the king and his wife, and they would look out over it, stroll in it, eat, drink and take their midday rest there. King Ajab treated his neighbour Mazdaki well and was kind to him, but his wife Azbil envied him on account of that garden. She schemed to seize it from him, because she heard people often mention it and marvel at its beauty. She schemed to kill him, but the king forbade her from doing so, and she could find no way against him. Then it happened that the king set out on a distant journey and his absence was prolonged. His wife Azbil seized this opportunity. She gathered a group of people and ordered them to testify against Mazdaki that he had reviled her husband Ajab. They agreed to her demand. In that era, their law was that whoever reviled the king would be put to death once the evidence was established against him. So she summoned Mazdaki and said to him: "It has reached me that you have reviled the king." Mazdaki denied it. She then brought the witnesses, and they testified falsely against him. She ordered him killed and took his garden. Allah grew angry with them on account of the righteous servant. When the king returned from his journey, she informed him of the news. He said to her: "You have not done right, and I do not think we will prosper after him. He was our neighbour for a long time; we treated him well and held back harm from him because of his rights over us. Then you ended his neighbourly relationship in the worst way." She said: "I only became angry on your behalf and judged by your judgment." He said to her: "Would your forbearance not have been enough to make you protect his neighbourly rights?" She said: "What has happened has happened."

Then Allah the Exalted sent Ilyas to King Ajab and his people, and commanded him to inform them that Allah the Exalted had become angry for His friend when they killed him unjustly, and had sworn by Himself that if the two of them did not repent of their deed and did not return the garden to the heirs of Mazdaki, He would destroy them, meaning Ajab and his wife, inside the garden. He would leave them as two corpses lying in it until their bones were stripped bare of their flesh, and they would enjoy it only a little.

He said: So Ilyas came and told him what Allah the Exalted had revealed to him concerning his affair, his wife's affair, and the return of the garden. When the king heard that, his anger against him intensified. Then he said to him: "O Ilyas, by Allah, I do not see what you call to as anything but falsehood. I see that so-and-so and so-and-so (he named kings from among them who had worshipped idols) were only upon the same thing we are upon. They eat and enjoy themselves, enjoying their rule, and their worldly affairs are not diminished by that matter of theirs which you claim is false. We see no superiority for ourselves over them."

He said: The king intended to torture Ilyas and kill him. When Ilyas sensed the evil and the plot against him [[Addition from "B".]], he left him and went out from him, and he took refuge in the high peaks of the mountains. The king returned to the worship of Ba'l. Ilyas climbed to the most difficult and loftiest mountain and entered a cave in it.

It is said that he remained for seven years as a fugitive in fear, retreating to mountain ravines and caves, eating from the plants of the earth and the fruits of trees, while they searched for him, having placed watchers over him, but Allah concealed him. When seven years had passed, Allah permitted his appearance before them and the relief of his anger against them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, afflicted a son of Ajab who was the dearest of his children to him and the most like him. He fell gravely ill until he despaired of him. So he called upon his idol Ba'l. They had been enamoured of Ba'l and had exalted him to the point that they had appointed four hundred attendants (sadin, keepers of a shrine) for him. They assigned them to him and made them his prophets [[Omitted from "B".]]. The Shaytan (devil) would enter the belly of the idol and speak, and the four hundred would listen with their ears to what the Shaytan said. The Shaytan would whisper to them a law of error, and they would spread it among the people, who would act upon it, and they called them prophets.

When the son of the king's grave illness intensified, the king asked them to intercede with Ba'l and seek healing for his son from him. They called upon him, but he did not answer them. Allah prevented the Shaytan from being able to enter his belly, while they were striving in supplication to him. When this lasted long for them, they said to Ajab: "In the region of Shaam there are other gods. Send your prophets to them; perhaps they will intercede for you with your god Ba'l, for he is angry with you. Were it not for his anger with you, he would have answered you." Ajab said: "And for what reason has he become angry with me, when I obey him?" They said: "Because you did not kill Ilyas, and you neglected him until he escaped unharmed, while he disbelieves in your god." Ajab said: "How can I kill Ilyas when I am preoccupied from seeking him by my son's illness? Ilyas has no known location that can be targeted. If my son were healed, I would devote myself to seeking him until I found him and killed him, and so please my god."

Then he sent his four hundred prophets to the gods in Shaam, asking them to intercede with the king's idol so that it would heal his son. They set out until, when they were opposite the mountain in which Ilyas was, Allah the Exalted revealed to Ilyas, peace be upon him, that he should descend from the mountain, confront them and speak to them. He said to him: "Do not fear, for I will turn their evil away from you and cast terror into their hearts." Ilyas descended from the mountain. When he met them, he halted them. When they stopped, he said to them: "Allah the Exalted has sent me to you and to those behind you. So listen, O people, to the message of your Lord, so that you may convey it to your companion, then return to him and say to him: Allah the Exalted says to you: 'Do you not know, O Ajab, that I am Allah, there is no god but Me, the God of the Children of Israel, who created them, provided for them, gave them life and caused them to die? Your ignorance and lack of knowledge have led you to associate others with Me and to seek healing for your son from other than Me, from those who possess nothing for themselves except what I will. I have sworn by My name that I will indeed enrage you concerning your son, and I will cause him to die at this very moment, until you know that no one possesses anything for him besides Me.'"

When he had said this to them, they returned, filled with terror of him. When they came to the king, they informed him that Ilyas had descended upon them. He was a thin, tall man, who had become emaciated, his hair had fallen out and his skin had peeled. He wore a woollen cloak and a cloak which he had fastened on his chest with thorns. "He halted us, and when he came among us, awe and terror of him were cast into our hearts, so our tongues were cut off, even though we were in this large number. We were unable to speak with him or answer him until we returned to you." They related to him the words of Ilyas. Ajab said: "We will not benefit from life as long as Ilyas is alive, and he can only be overcome through deception and treachery." He appointed for him fifty men of his people, who were strong and valiant, entrusted them with his covenant and commanded them to scheme against him, to assassinate him, and to make him believe that they, and those behind them, had believed in him, so that he would feel secure with them, be deceived by them, allow them to approach him, and they would bring him to their king. They set out until they climbed that mountain in which Ilyas was. Then they spread out upon it, calling out to him at the top of their voices, saying: "O Prophet of Allah, come out to us and bestow your favour upon us by showing yourself. We have believed in you and affirmed you. Our king Ajab and all our people are with us, and you are safe for yourself. All the Children of Israel send you greetings and say: 'Your message has reached us and we have understood what you said. [[Addition from "B".]] We have believed in you, answered you in what you called us to, so come to us, dwell among us and judge among us.' We will submit to what you command us and refrain from what you forbid us. It is not fitting for you to remain apart from us, given our faith and obedience, so return to us." All of this from them was deceit and treachery.

فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ إِلْيَاسُ مَقَالَتَهُمْ وَقَعَتْ فِي قَلْبِهِ وَطَمِعَ فِي إِيمَانِهِمْ، وَخَافَ اللَّهَ إِنْ هُوَ لَمْ يَظْهَرْ لَهُمْ، فَأَلْهَمَهُ اللَّهُ التَّوَقُّفَ وَالدُّعَاءَ، فَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ فِيمَا يَقُولُونَ فَأْذَنْ لِي فِي الْبُرُوزِ إِلَيْهِمْ، وَإِنْ كَانُوا كَاذِبِينَ فَاكْفِنِيهِمْ وَارْمِهِمْ بِنَارٍ تَحْرِقُهُمْ، فَمَا اسْتَتَمَّ قَوْلَهُ حَتَّى حُصِبُوا بِالنَّارِ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ، فَاحْتَرَقُوا أَجْمَعِينَ. قَالَ: وَبَلَغَ آجَبَ الْخَبَرُ فَلَمْ يَرْتَدِعْ مِنْ هَمِّهِ بِالسُّوءِ، وَاحْتَالَ ثَانِيًا فِي أَمْرِ إِلْيَاسَ، وَقَيَّضَ لَهُ فِئَةً أُخْرَى مِثْلَ عَدَدِ أُولَئِكَ أَقْوَى مِنْهُمْ وَأَمْكَنُ مِنَ الْحِيلَةِ وَالرَّأْيِ، فَأَقْبَلُوا، أَيْ: حَتَّى تَوَقَّلُوا، أَيْ: صَعَدُوا قُلَلَ تِلْكَ الْجِبَالِ مُتَفَرِّقِينَ، وَجَعَلُوا يُنَادُونَ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ إِنَّا نُعَوِّذُ بِاللَّهِ وَبِكَ مِنْ غَضَبِ اللَّهِ وَسَطَوَاتِهِ، إِنَّا لَسْنَا كَالَّذِينَ أَتَوْكَ قَبْلَنَا، وَإِنَّ أُولَئِكَ فِرْقَةٌ نَافَقُوا فَصَارُوا إِلَيْكَ لِيَكِيدُوا بِكَ فِي غَيْرِ رَأْيِنَا، وَلَوْ عَلِمْنَا بِهِمْ لَقَتَلْنَاهُمْ وَلَكَفَيْنَاكَ مُؤْنَتَهُمْ، فَالْآنَ قَدْ كَفَاكَ رَبُّكَ أَمْرَهُمْ وَأَهْلَكَهُمْ وَانْتَقَمَ لَنَا وَلَكَ مِنْهُمْ. فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ إِلْيَاسُ مَقَالَتَهُمْ دَعَا اللَّهَ بِدَعْوَتِهِ الْأُولَى فَأَمْطَرَ عَلَيْهِمُ النَّارَ، فَاحْتَرَقُوا عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ. وَفِي كُلِّ ذَلِكَ ابْنُ الْمَلِكِ فِي الْبَلَاءِ الشَّدِيدِ مِنْ وَجَعِهِ، فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ بِهَلَاكِ أَصْحَابِهِ ثَانِيًا ازْدَادَ غَضَبًا عَلَى غَضَبٍ، وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ فِي طَلَبِ إِلْيَاسَ بِنَفْسِهِ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ شَغَلَهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ مَرَضُ ابْنِهِ، فَلَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ، فَوَجَّهَ نَحْوَ إِلْيَاسَ الْمُؤْمِنَ الَّذِي هُوَ كَاتِبُ امْرَأَتِهِ، رَجَاءَ أَنْ يَأْنَسَ بِهِ إِلْيَاسُ فَيَنْزِلَ مَعَهُ، وَأَظْهَرَ لِلْكَاتِبِ أَنَّهُ لَا يُرِيدُ بِإِلْيَاسَ سُوءًا، وَإِنَّمَا أَظْهَرَ لَهُ لِمَا اطَّلَعَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ إِيمَانِهِ، وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ مَعَ اطِّلَاعِهِ عَلَى إِيمَانِهِ مُغْضِيًا عَلَيْهِ لِمَا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِفَايَةِ وَالْأَمَانَةِ وَسَدَادِ الرَّأْيِ، فَلَمَّا وَجَّهَهُ نَحْوَهُ أَرْسَلَ مَعَهُ فِئَةً مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ، وَأَوْعَزَ إِلَى الْفِئَةِ -دُونَ الْكَاتِبِ- أَنْ يُوثِقُوا إِلْيَاسَ وَيَأْتُوا بِهِ إِنْ أَرَادَ التَّخَلُّفَ عَنْهُمْ، وَإِنْ جَاءَ مَعَ الْكَاتِبِ وَاثِقًا بِهِ لَمْ يُرَوِّعُوهُ. ثُمَّ أَظْهَرَ مَعَ الْكَاتِبِ الْإِنَابَةَ وَقَالَ لَهُ: قَدْ آنَ لِي أَنْ أَتُوبَ، وَقَدْ أَصَابَتْنَا بَلَايَا مِنْ حَرِيقِ أَصْحَابِنَا وَالْبَلَاءِ الَّذِي فِيهِ ابْنِي، وَقَدْ عَرَفْتُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ بِدَعْوَةِ إِلْيَاسَ، وَلَسْتُ آمَنُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ مَنْ بَقِيَ مِنَّا فَنَهْلَكَ بِدَعْوَتِهِ، فَانْطَلِقْ إِلَيْهِ وَأَخْبِرْهُ أَنَّا قَدْ تُبْنَا وَأَنَبْنَا، وَأَنَّهُ لَا يُصْلِحُنَا فِي تَوْبَتِنَا، وَمَا نُرِيدُ مِنْ رِضَاءِ رَبِّنَا وَخَلْعِ أَصْنَامِنَا إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ إِلْيَاسُ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِنَا، يَأْمُرُنَا وَيَنْهَانَا، وَيُخْبِرُنَا بِمَا يُرْضِي رَبَّنَا. وَأَمَرَ قَوْمَهُ فَاعْتَزَلُوا الْأَصْنَامَ، وَقَالَ لَهُ: أَخْبِرْ إِلْيَاسَ أَنَّا قَدْ خَلَعْنَا آلِهَتَنَا الَّتِي كُنَّا نَعْبُدُ، وَأَرْجَأْنَا أَمْرَهَا حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ إِلْيَاسُ فَيَكُونَ هُوَ الَّذِي يَحْرِقُهَا وَيُهْلِكُهَا، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ مَكْرًا مِنَ الْمَلِكِ.

فَانْطَلَقَ الْكَاتِبُ وَالْفِئَةُ حَتَّى عَلَا الْجَبَلَ الَّذِي فِيهِ إِلْيَاسُ ثُمَّ نَادَاهُ، فَعَرَفَ إِلْيَاسُ صَوْتَهُ، فَتَاقَتْ نَفْسُهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ مُشْتَاقًا إِلَى لِقَائِهِ، فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِلَيْهِ: أَنِ ابْرُزْ إِلَى أَخِيكَ الصَّالِحِ فَالْقَهُ وَجَدِّدِ الْعَهْدَ بِهِ، فَبَرَزَ إِلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَصَافَحَهُ، وَقَالَ لَهُ: مَا الْخَبَرُ؟ فَقَالَ الْمُؤْمِنُ: إِنَّهُ قَدْ بَعَثَنِي إِلَيْكَ هَذَا الْجَبَّارُ الطَّاغِيَةُ وَقَوْمُهُ، ثُمَّ قَصَّ عَلَيْهِ مَا قَالُوا، ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ: وَإِنِّي لَخَائِفٌ إِنْ رَجَعْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَلَسْتَ مَعِي أَنْ يَقْتُلَنِي، فَمُرْنِي بِمَا شِئْتَ أَفْعَلْهُ: إِنْ شِئْتَ انْقَطَعْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَكُنْتُ مَعَكَ وَتَرَكْتُهُ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ جَاهَدْتُهُ مَعَكَ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ تُرْسِلُنِي إِلَيْهِ بِمَا تُحِبُّ فَأُبَلِّغَهُ رِسَالَتَكَ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ دَعَوْتَ رَبَّكَ يَجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا فَرَجًا وَمَخْرَجًا. فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِلَى إِلْيَاسَ أَنَّ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ جَاءَكَ مِنْهُمْ مَكْرٌ وَكَذِبٌ لِيَظْفَرُوا بِكَ، وَإِنَّ آجَبَ إِنْ أَخْبَرَتْهُ رُسُلُهُ أَنَّكَ قَدْ لَقِيتَ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ وَلَمْ يَأْتِ بِكَ اتَّهَمَهُ وَعَرَفَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ دَاهَنَ فِي أَمْرِكَ، فَلَمْ يَأْمَنْ أَنْ يَقْتُلَهُ، فَانْطَلِقْ مَعَهُ فَإِنِّي سَأُشْغِلُ عَنْكُمَا آجَبَ فَأُضَاعِفُ عَلَى ابْنِهِ الْبَلَاءَ، حَتَّى لَا يَكُونَ لَهُ هَمٌّ غَيْرُهُ، ثُمَّ أُمِيتُهُ عَلَى شَرِّ حَالٍ، فَإِذَا مَاتَ فَارْجِعْ عَنْهُ. قَالَ: فَانْطَلَقَ مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى قَدِمُوا عَلَى آجَبَ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمُوا شَدَّدَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى الْوَجَعَ عَلَى ابْنِهِ وَأَخَذَ الْمَوْتُ يَكْظِمُهُ، فَشَغَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِذَلِكَ آجَبَ وَأَصْحَابَهُ عَنْ إِلْيَاسَ، فَرَجَعَ إِلْيَاسُ سَالِمًا إِلَى مَكَانِهِ. فَلَمَّا مَاتَ ابْنُ آجَبَ وَفَرَغُوا مِنْ أَمْرِهِ وَقَلَّ جَزَعُهُ انْتَبَهَ لِإِلْيَاسَ، وَسَأَلَ عَنْهُ الْكَاتِبَ الَّذِي جَاءَ بِهِ، فَقَالَ: لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ، شَغَلَنِي عَنْهُ مَوْتُ ابْنِكَ وَالْجَزَعُ عَلَيْهِ، وَلَمْ أَكُنْ أَحْسَبُكَ إِلَّا قَدِ اسْتَوْثَقْتَ مِنْهُ، فَانْصَرَفَ عَنْهُ آجَبُ وَتَرَكَهُ لِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ عَلَى ابْنِهِ.

فَلَمَّا طَالَ الْأَمْرُ عَلَى إِلْيَاسَ مَلَّ السُّكُونَ فِي الْجِبَالِ وَاشْتَاقَ إِلَى النَّاسِ، نَزَلَ مِنَ الْجَبَلِ فَانْطَلَقَ حَتَّى نَزَلَ بِامْرَأَةٍ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ، وَهِيَ أُمُّ يُونُسَ بْنِ مَتَّى ذِي النُّونِ [98أ]، فَاسْتَخْفَى عِنْدَهَا سِتَّةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَيُونُسُ بْنُ مَتَّى يَوْمَئِذٍ مَوْلُودٌ يَرْضَعُ، فَكَانَتْ أُمُّ يُونُسَ تَخْدِمُهُ بِنَفْسِهَا وَتُوَاسِيهِ بِذَاتِ يَدِهَا. ثُمَّ إِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ سَئِمَ ضِيقَ الْبُيُوتِ بَعْدَ تَعَوُّدِهِ فُسْحَةَ الْجِبَالِ، فَأَحَبَّ اللُّحُوقَ بِالْجِبَالِ، فَخَرَجَ وَعَادَ إِلَى مَكَانِهِ، فَجَزِعَتْ أُمُّ يُونُسَ لِفِرَاقِهِ فَأَوْحَشَهَا فَقْدُهُ. ثُمَّ لَمْ تَلْبَثْ إِلَّا يَسِيرًا حَتَّى مَاتَ ابْنُهَا يُونُسُ حِينَ فَطَمَتْهُ، فَعَظُمَتْ مُصِيبَتُهَا فَخَرَجَتْ فِي طَلَبِ إِلْيَاسَ، فَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَرْقَى الْجِبَالَ وَتَطُوفُ فِيهَا حَتَّى عَثَرَتْ عَلَيْهِ، فَوَجَدَتْهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ: إِنِّي قَدْ فُجِعْتُ بَعْدَكَ لِمَوْتِ ابْنِي، فَعَظُمَتْ فِيهِ مُصِيبَتِي وَاشْتَدَّ لِفَقْدِهِ بَلَائِي، وَلَيْسَ لِي وَلَدٌ غَيْرُهُ، فَارْحَمْنِي وَادْعُ لِي رَبَّكَ جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ لِيُحْيِيَ لِي ابْنِي، وَإِنِّي قَدْ تَرَكْتُهُ مُسَجًّى لَمْ أَدْفِنْهُ، وَقَدْ أَخْفَيْتُ مَكَانَهُ. فَقَالَ لَهَا إِلْيَاسُ: لَيْسَ هَذَا مِمَّا أُمِرْتُ بِهِ، وَإِنَّمَا أَنَا عَبْدٌ مَأْمُورٌ أَعْمَلُ بِمَا يَأْمُرُنِي رَبِّي، فَجَزِعَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ وَتَضَرَّعَتْ، فَأَعْطَفَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَلْبَ إِلْيَاسَ لَهَا، فَقَالَ لَهَا: مَتَى مَاتَ ابْنُكِ؟ قَالَتْ: مُنْذُ سَبْعَةِ أَيَّامٍ، فَانْطَلَقَ إِلْيَاسُ مَعَهَا وَسَارَ سَبْعَةَ أَيَّامٍ أُخْرَى حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى مَنْزِلِهَا، فَوَجَدَ ابْنَهَا مَيِّتًا لَهُ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا، فَتَوَضَّأَ وَصَلَّى وَدَعَا، فَأَحْيَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى يُونُسَ بْنَ مَتَّى، فَلَمَّا عَاشَ وَجَلَسَ وَثَبَ إِلْيَاسُ وَتَرَكَهُ وَعَادَ إِلَى مَوْضِعِهِ.

فَلَمَّا طَالَ عِصْيَانُ قَوْمِهِ ضَاقَ بِذَلِكَ إِلْيَاسُ ذَرْعًا، فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ وَهُوَ خَائِفٌ مَجْهُودٌ: يَا إِلْيَاسُ مَا هَذَا الْحُزْنُ وَالْجَزَعُ الَّذِي أَنْتَ فِيهِ؟ أَلَسْتَ أَمِينِي عَلَى وَحْيِي وَحُجَّتِي فِي أَرْضِي وَصَفْوَتِي مِنْ خَلْقِي؟ فَسَلْنِي أُعْطِكَ، فَإِنِّي ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ الْوَاسِعَةِ وَالْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ. قَالَ: تُمِيتُنِي وَتُلْحِقُنِي بِآبَائِي، فَإِنِّي قَدْ مَلِلْتُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَمَلُّونِي. فَأَوْحَى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِلَيْهِ: يَا إِلْيَاسُ مَا هَذَا بِالْيَوْمِ الَّذِي أُعَرِّي فِيهِ عَنْكَ الْأَرْضَ وَأَهْلَهَا، وَإِنَّمَا قِوَامُهَا وَصَلَاحُهَا بِكَ وَبِأَشْبَاهِكَ، وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ قَلِيلًا، وَلَكِنْ سَلْنِي فَأُعْطِكَ. فَقَالَ إِلْيَاسُ: إِنْ لَمْ تُمِتْنِي فَأَعْطِنِي ثَأْرِي مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: فَأَيُّ شَيْءٍ تُرِيدُ أَنْ أُعْطِيَكَ؟ قَالَ: تُمَكِّنُنِي مِنْ خَزَائِنِ السَّمَاءِ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ، فَلَا تَنْشُرُ عَلَيْهِمْ سَحَابَةً إِلَّا بِدَعْوَتِي، وَلَا تُمْطِرُ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ قَطْرَةً إِلَّا بِشَفَاعَتِي، فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُذِلُّهُمْ إِلَّا ذَلِكَ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: يَا إِلْيَاسُ أَنَا أَرْحَمُ بِخَلْقِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ كَانُوا ظَالِمِينَ. قَالَ: فَسِتُّ سِنِينَ. قَالَ: أَنَا أَرْحَمُ بِخَلْقِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ. قَالَ: فَخَمْسُ سِنِينَ. قَالَ: أَنَا أَرْحَمُ بِخَلْقِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَلَكِنِّي أُعْطِيكَ ثَأْرَكَ ثَلَاثَ سِنِينَ، أَجْعَلُ خَزَائِنَ الْمَطَرِ بِيَدِكَ. قَالَ إِلْيَاسُ: فَبِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ أَعِيشُ؟ قَالَ: أُسَخِّرُ لَكَ جَيْشًا مِنَ الطَّيْرِ يَنْقُلُ إِلَيْكَ طَعَامَكَ وَشَرَابَكَ مِنَ الرِّيفِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّتِي لَمْ تَقْحَطْ. قَالَ إِلْيَاسُ: قَدْ رَضِيتُ. قَالَ: فَأَمْسَكَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُمُ الْمَطَرَ حَتَّى هَلَكَتِ الْمَاشِيَةُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَالْهَوَامُّ وَالشَّجَرُ، وَجَهِدَ النَّاسُ جُهْدًا شَدِيدًا، وَإِلْيَاسُ عَلَى حَالَتِهِ مُسْتَخْفٍ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ، يُوضَعُ لَهُ الرِّزْقُ حَيْثُ مَا كَانَ، وَقَدْ عَرَفَ ذَلِكَ قَوْمُهُ، وَكَانُوا إِذَا وَجَدُوا رِيحَ الْخُبْزِ فِي بَيْتٍ قَالُوا: لَقَدْ دَخَلَ إِلْيَاسُ هَذَا الْمَكَانَ، وَطَلَبُوهُ وَلَقِيَ مِنْ أَهْلِ ذَلِكَ الْمَنْزِلِ شَرًّا.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Children of Israel were struck by famine for three years. Ilyas (Elijah) passed by an old woman and said to her, "Do you have any food?" She said, "Yes, a little flour and a little oil." He said, "Bring them to me," and he invoked blessing upon them and touched them until he filled her sack with flour and her jars with oil. When they saw this with her, they said, "From where do you have this?" She said, "A man passed by me, of such and such a condition," and she described him by his description, so they recognized him. They said, "That is Ilyas." They sought him and found him, but he fled from them. Then he took refuge in the house of a woman from the Children of Israel who had a son called al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, who had an affliction. She sheltered him and concealed his affair. He prayed for the boy, and he was healed from the affliction he had. Al-Yasa' followed Ilyas, believed in him, affirmed him, and remained with him, going wherever he went. Ilyas had grown old and advanced in years, while al-Yasa' was young. Then Allah the Exalted revealed to Ilyas: "You have destroyed many of the creation, including beasts, animals, birds and insects, by withholding the rain." So they claim, and Allah knows best, that Ilyas said, "My Lord, let me be the one who calls upon them and brings them relief from the trial they are in, perhaps they will return and abandon what they are upon of worshipping other than You." It was said to him, "Yes." So Ilyas came to the Children of Israel and said, "You have perished from hunger and hardship, and the beasts, animals, birds, insects and trees have perished because of your sins. You are upon falsehood. If you wish to know this, then go out with your idols. If they respond to you, then it is as you say; but if they do not do so, you will know that you are upon falsehood, and you will desist, and I will call upon Allah the Exalted, and He will relieve you of the trial you are in." They said, "You have been just." So they went out with their idols and called upon them, but they did not relieve them of the trial they were in. Then they said to Ilyas, "We have perished, so call upon Allah the Exalted for us." Ilyas prayed for them, and with him was al-Yasa', for relief. A cloud like a shield came out over the surface of the sea while they were watching. It advanced toward them and covered the horizons. Then Allah the Exalted sent down the rain upon them, and it gave them relief, and their lands were revived. But when Allah the Exalted removed the harm from them, they broke the covenant and did not desist from their disbelief, and they persisted in the most wicked of what they had been upon. When Ilyas saw this, he called upon his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to relieve him of them. It was said to him, as they claim: "Look at such and such a day, and go out on it to such and such a place. Whatever comes to you, mount it and do not turn it away." So Ilyas went out, and with him was al-Yasa', until when they were at the place where he had been commanded, a horse of fire came forward, and it was said: its color was like the color of fire, until it stood before him. Ilyas leapt upon it, and the horse carried him away. Al-Yasa' called out to him, "O Ilyas, what do you command me?" Ilyas threw to him his cloak from the highest atmosphere. That was the sign of his succession over the Children of Israel, and that was the last covenant with him. Allah the Exalted raised Ilyas from among them, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and clothed him with plumage. So he became human, angelic, earthly and heavenly. Allah the Exalted empowered against Ahab the king and his people an enemy of theirs, who came upon them from a place they did not perceive, until he overwhelmed them. He killed Ahab and his wife Izabel in the garden of a man named Mazdaki. Their two corpses remained lying in that garden until their flesh decayed and their bones crumbled. Allah the Exalted made al-Yasa' a prophet and sent him as a messenger to the Children of Israel, and Allah the Exalted revealed to him and supported him. The Children of Israel believed in him, and they used to venerate him, and the judgment of Allah the Exalted among them remained in force until al-Yasa' departed from them. [[Al-Tabari narrated the story through the chain of Ibn Ishaq in al-Tarikh: 1/461–464. He abridged it in the Tafsir: 23/93–94.]] .

And al-Sarri ibn Yahya narrated from Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, who said: al-Khidr and Ilyas fast the month of Ramadan in Bayt al-Maqdis, and they attend the season (al-mawsim) every year.

It is said: Ilyas is entrusted with the deserts (al-fayafi), and al-Khidr is entrusted with the seas [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/118.]]. This is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers﴾.

﴿When he said to his people, "Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon﴾ Do you worship [[addition from "b"]] ﴿Ba'l﴾, which was the name of an idol they worshipped. For this reason their city was named Ba'labakk." Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: "al-Ba'l" (the lord) in the dialect of the people of Yemen means "the lord."

﴿And you forsake the best of creators﴾, so you do not keep away from Him.

﴿Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old﴾. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Ya'qub read "Allah, your Lord and the Lord" with the ha' and the two ba's in the accusative, as a badal (substitution or apposition). The others read them in the nominative, as an istina' (a new, resumptive sentence).

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought forth﴾ into the Fire.

﴿Except the chosen servants of Allah﴾ from among his people, for they were saved from the punishment.

﴿And We left for him among later generations: "Peace be upon the family of Yasin."﴾ Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "آلِ يَاسِينَ" (Ālu Yāsīn) with a lengthened fatha on the hamza and a broken (separated) kasra on the lam, because in the Mushaf it is written separately. [The others read it with a kasra on the hamza and a sukun on the lam, joined (mawsulah).] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]]

As for the one who reads "آلِ يس" as separated, it has been said that he meant the family of Muhammad (ﷺ). This view is weak, because no previous mention of him has preceded it. It has also been said that he meant the family of Ilyas.

The well-known reading is the joined one, and they differed about it. It has been said that Ilyasin is a dialectal form (lughah) of Ilyas, like Isma'il and Isma'in, and Mika'il and Mika'in.

Al-Farra' said: it is a plural, meaning Ilyas and his followers among the believers, so it is in the position of al-Ash'arin and al-A'jamin with the lightened form. In the reading of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Salamun 'ala Idrasin," meaning Idris and his followers, because he reads: "And indeed Idris was among the messengers." [[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 2/391–392.]]

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants. And indeed Lut was among the messengers. When We saved him and his family, all of them, except an old woman who was among those who remained behind.﴾ That is: those who remained in the punishment.

﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ And tadmir (destruction) means annihilation.

﴿And indeed you pass by them﴾ over their traces and dwelling places, ﴿in the morning﴾ at the time of morning,

﴿and at night.﴾ He means: you pass by them by day and by night when you go off on your journeys and return. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ So that you may take warning from them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed Yunus was among the messengers.﴾ He was one of the messengers of God.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 140–145:**

﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾. That is: he ran away (abaqa).

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) and Wahb said: Yunus had promised his people the punishment, but when the punishment was delayed from them, he went out from among them in a state of shame (al-mashur: the embarrassed one; in manuscript "A" it reads al-mutashur). He headed for the sea and boarded a ship. The ship stopped moving, and the sailors said: "There is a runaway slave here who has fled from his master." They drew lots, and the lot fell upon Yunus. They drew lots three times, and it fell upon Yunus each time. Yunus said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water.

It is related in the story that when he reached the sea, his wife and two sons were with him. A boat came, and he wanted to board with them, so he sent his wife ahead to board before him. A wave came between him and the boat, and the boat passed by. Then another wave came and took his elder son, and a wolf came and took his younger son, so he remained alone. Another boat came and he boarded it, sitting in a corner among the people. When the ship had moved along in the sea, it became still, so they drew lots. We have mentioned the story in the commentary on Surah Yunus (see above: 4/151–152).

That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So he cast lots﴾, that is, he drew lots with them. Musahama is casting arrows by way of lots. ﴿And he was among the losers﴾, those who lost the draw.

﴿Then the fish swallowed him﴾: it swallowed him, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾: one who had done what deserved blame.

﴿Had he not been of those who glorify [Allah]﴾: of those who remembered Allah before that, and he used to remember Him often. Ibn ʿAbbas said: of those who pray. Wahb said: of those who worship. Al-Hasan said: He had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had previously done righteous deeds. Al-Dahhak said: Allah, the Exalted, was grateful to him for his earlier obedience.

It was also said: "Had he not been of those who glorify [Allah]" refers to [his glorification] in the belly of the fish. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: it refers to his saying: "There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers" [al-Anbiya': 87].

﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾: the belly of the fish would have become his grave until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿So We cast him﴾: We threw him, ﴿onto the open shore﴾: that is, onto the surface of the earth. Al-Suddi said: onto the coast. Al-ʿAra' is land free of trees and vegetation. ﴿while he was ill﴾: sick, like a featherless young bird. It was also said: his flesh had decayed, his bones had become thin, and he had no strength left.

They differed regarding the length of his stay in the belly of the fish. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. ʿAta' said: seven days. Al-Dahhak said: twenty days. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: forty days. Al-Shaʿbi said: it swallowed him in the forenoon and expelled him in the evening. [[The Suyuti mentioned these sayings in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/127.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 146–147:**

﴿And We caused to grow over him﴾, i.e., for him. It is also said: beside him, ﴿a tree of gourd (yaqtin)﴾. Yaqtin means the pumpkin (qar'), according to the view of all the commentators (mufassirun).

Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: Yaqtin is every plant that spreads and extends over the surface of the earth, has no stalk, and does not survive the winter, such as the pumpkin, the cucumber, and the watermelon.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Yunus used to shelter under the tree, and a female wild goat (wa'la) would come to him, and he would drink from her milk morning and evening until his flesh became firm, his hair grew, and he became strong. Then he slept a sleep, and when he awoke the tree had withered. He grieved a great grief, and the heat of the sun afflicted him, so he began to weep. Allah the Exalted sent Jibril to him and said: "Do you grieve over a tree, and do not grieve over one hundred thousand of your community, who have embraced Islam and repented?" [[See: al-Tabari: 23/103–104.]]

If it is asked: Here He said, ﴿So We cast him onto the open land while he was sick﴾, and in another place He said, ﴿Had not a favour from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast onto the open land (bil-'ara') in disgrace﴾ (Surah al-Qalam: 49). Does this not indicate that he was not cast out?

It is answered: The "lawla" (had it not been) there refers to blame. Its meaning is: Had it not been for a favour from his Lord, he would have been cast onto the open land while he was blameworthy. But the favour reached him, so he was cast out while not blameworthy.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And We sent him to one hundred thousand﴾. Qatadah said: He was sent to the people of Nineveh (Ninawa) in the land of Mosul, before what befell him had befallen him. His saying ﴿And We sent him﴾ means: and We had indeed sent him. It is also said: his sending was after his emergence from the belly of the fish to them. And it is said: it was to another people.

﴿Or they increase﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is "and they increase"; "aw" (or) here carries the meaning of "wa" (and), as in His saying, ﴿excuse or warning﴾ (Surah al-Mursalat: 6). Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: its meaning is "bal" (rather), that is, "rather they increase."

Al-Zajjaj said: "aw" here is in its original sense, and its meaning is: "or they increase beyond your estimate and your assumption," like a man who sees a group of people and says: "These are a thousand, or more." The doubt is with regard to the estimation of the created beings. Most of them hold that its meaning is "and they increase."

They differed concerning the extent of that increase. Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: they were twenty thousand. This was narrated by Ubayy ibn Ka'b from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir: 9/97, and he said: "This is a strange (gharib) hadith." Al-Mubarakfuri said: "Its chain contains an unknown narrator." Also al-Tabari: 23/104. Al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/132, also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

Al-Hasan said: thirty-odd thousand.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: seventy thousand. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 23/104; al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/132, attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verse 148–156:

﴿So they believed﴾, meaning: those to whom Yunus (Jonah) was sent, after witnessing the punishment, ﴿so We let them enjoy for a time﴾, until the end of their appointed terms.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So ask them﴾, meaning: ask them, O Muhammad, the people of Makkah, and this is a question of reproach, ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾ This is because Juhaynah and the Banu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/133.]]. The meaning is: they attributed daughters to Allah and sons to themselves.

﴿Or did We create the angels as females﴾, its meaning: did We create the angels as females, ﴿while they were witnesses?﴾, present at Our creating them. Its parallel is His saying: "Did they witness their creation?" [al-Zukhruf: 19].

﴿Surely it is of their falsehood﴾, of their lying, ﴿that they say: "Allah has begotten." And indeed they are liars.﴾

﴿Has He chosen﴾: Abu Ja'far read: "They are liars. Ist̤afā" joined, as a report of the statement of the polytheists, and when pausing, he begins: "ists̤afā" with a kasra on the alif. The common reading is with an alif cut (hamzat al-qat'), because it is an interrogative alif that entered upon the alif of wasl (connection), so the alif of wasl was dropped and the interrogative alif remained open and cut, like: astakbara and the like, ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾.

﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾, that for Allah are daughters and for you are sons.

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾, will you not then admonish yourselves.

﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾, a manifest proof that Allah has a son.

We have also related from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The sky has creaked, and it has a right to creak. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 165–173:

﴿And indeed, We are the ones who stand in ranks.﴾ Qatadah said: "They are the angels, who align their feet." Al-Kalbi said: "The rows of the angels in the heaven for worship are like the rows of people on the earth."

﴿And indeed, We are the ones who glorify (Allah).﴾ That is, those who pray and who declare Allah far exalted above evil. Jibril (peace be upon him) informs [the Prophet (ﷺ)] that they worship Allah through prayer and glorification, and that they are not objects of worship, as the disbelievers claimed. Then he returned the speech to informing about the polytheists, saying:

﴿And indeed, they used to say﴾ — and they had been saying, that is, the people of Makkah — ﴿"If only we had a reminder from the former peoples,﴾ — the lam here is the lam of emphasis.

﴿we would have been sincere servants of Allah."﴾ That is, a Book like the Book of the former peoples. ﴿But they disbelieved in it,﴾ that is, when that Book came to them, they disbelieved in it. ﴿So they will soon know.﴾ This is a warning to them.

﴿And indeed Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers,﴾ and it is His saying: "Allah has decreed: 'I and My messengers will surely prevail.'" (al-Mujadilah: 21)

﴿Indeed, they will be the ones given victory, and indeed, Our soldiers will be the ones who prevail.﴾ That is, the party of Allah will have victory through proof and through support in the end.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 174–182:

﴿So turn away﴾, i.e., withdraw ﴿from them for a time﴾. Ibn Abbas said: it means death. Mujahid said: the day of Badr. Al-Suddi said: until We command you to fight. It was also said: until God's punishment comes upon them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of fighting. [[See above: 3/32 note (1), 3/273 note (1). Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 2/396.]]

﴿And watch them﴾, i.e., when the punishment descends upon them, ﴿for they will see﴾ that, and they said: "When is this punishment?"

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment? * But when it descends upon their courtyard﴾, meaning the punishment. Muqatil said: "in their presence." It was also said: "at their threshold." Al-Farra' said: "The Arabs suffice by mentioning the courtyard instead of the people." ﴿Evil is the morning of those warned﴾, i.e., evil is the morning of the disbelievers who were warned of the punishment.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, Malik informed us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik: When the Messenger of God ﷺ set out for Khaybar, he came upon it at night, and whenever he came upon a people at night, he would not attack until morning. He said: When morning came, the Jews of Khaybar came out with their hoes and baskets. When they saw the Prophet ﷺ, they said: "Muhammad, by God, Muhammad and the army!" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God is greatest, Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those warned." [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta, chapter on what has come concerning horses: 2/468; al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter: what blood is protected by the call to prayer: 2/89-90; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter: the raid of Khaybar, no. 1365, 3/1426-1427; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/59.]]

Then he repeated what we have mentioned, to emphasize the threat of punishment, saying:

﴿And turn away from them for a time * And watch﴾ the punishment when it descends upon them, ﴿for they will see﴾. Then He declared Himself free of imperfection, saying:

﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might﴾, the Overpowering and the Strong, ﴿above what they describe﴾ of taking consorts and children.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, who conveyed from God the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and the laws.

﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, for the destruction of the enemies and the victory of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan informed us, Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyya, from Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from Ali who said: "Whoever wishes to be measured with the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let the last of his words from his gathering be: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." [[Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir: 4/26, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim as a mursal (broken-chain) report, and said: it was narrated by another connected route, stopping at Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he cited it from the narration of the author. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/141 to Humayd ibn Zanjawayh in his al-Targhib. In the hadith is Asbagh ibn Nubatah. Abu Hatim said in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil: 2/320: "weak in narration (lin al-hadith)." Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing."]] [[In copy "A": The third volume is completed, by the praise of God and His good guidance.]]

[[Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir: 4/26, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim as a mursal (broken-chain) report, and said: it was narrated by another connected route, stopping at Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he cited it from the narration of the author. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/141 to Humayd ibn Zanjawayh in his al-Targhib. In the hadith is Asbagh ibn Nubatah. Abu Hatim said in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil: 2/320: "weak in narration (lin al-hadith)." Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing."]] [[In copy "A": The third volume is completed, by the praise of God and His good guidance.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 174–182:

﴿So turn away﴾, i.e., withdraw ﴿from them for a time﴾. Ibn Abbas said: it means death. Mujahid said: the day of Badr. Al-Suddi said: until We command you to fight. It was also said: until God's punishment comes upon them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of fighting. [[See above: 3/32 note (1), 3/273 note (1). Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 2/396.]]

﴿And watch them﴾, i.e., when the punishment descends upon them, ﴿for they will see﴾ that, and they said: "When is this punishment?"

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment? * But when it descends upon their courtyard﴾, meaning the punishment. Muqatil said: "in their presence." It was also said: "at their threshold." Al-Farra' said: "The Arabs suffice by mentioning the courtyard instead of the people." ﴿Evil is the morning of those warned﴾, i.e., evil is the morning of the disbelievers who were warned of the punishment.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, Malik informed us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik: When the Messenger of God ﷺ set out for Khaybar, he came upon it at night, and whenever he came upon a people at night, he would not attack until morning. He said: When morning came, the Jews of Khaybar came out with their hoes and baskets. When they saw the Prophet ﷺ, they said: "Muhammad, by God, Muhammad and the army!" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God is greatest, Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those warned." [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta, chapter on what has come concerning horses: 2/468; al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter: what blood is protected by the call to prayer: 2/89-90; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter: the raid of Khaybar, no. 1365, 3/1426-1427; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/59.]]

Then he repeated what we have mentioned, to emphasize the threat of punishment, saying:

﴿And turn away from them for a time * And watch﴾ the punishment when it descends upon them, ﴿for they will see﴾. Then He declared Himself free of imperfection, saying:

﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might﴾, the Overpowering and the Strong, ﴿above what they describe﴾ of taking consorts and children.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾, who conveyed from God the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and the laws.

﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, for the destruction of the enemies and the victory of the prophets, peace be upon them.
